steps.body: Every sinusoid is y = **A** sin(**B**(x − **C**)) + **D**: amplitude A (recall), period 2π/B (recall), phase shift C (new), midline D (recall). Four independent dials. To graph: draw the midline, mark the amplitude band, start a sine shape at x = C, and fit one period of length 2π/B.

predict.prompt: y = 3 sin(2(x − 45°)) + 1. Which dial decides the MAXIMUM value of y?

options.label: The 2 inside — it doubles the height

predict.reveal: Amplitude sets how far the wave swings, the midline sets what it swings AROUND: max = 1 + 3 = 4. The 2 inside changes how fast, never how high. Set the four dials and watch each one move exactly one thing.

widget.prompt: Reproduce y = 3 sin(2(x − 45°)) + 1: set each dial and watch what it — and only it — changes, until your wave sits on the dashed target.

dials.feedback: The swing is wrong. Amplitude is the distance from the midline to the crest — this wave rises 3 above its center line, not to 3.
The wave repeats at the wrong rate. The 2 multiplies the ANGLE, so the trace advances twice as fast per degree of drag — watch the tip lap the target.
The slide is off. 2(x − 45°) = 2x − 90°: the shift inside the brackets gets multiplied too, so the phase dial needs −90°, not −45° — the factored form hides a doubled delay.
The center line is wrong. The + 1 outside lifts the whole wave — crest, trough and axis together — up by one.

widget.successFeedback: All four dials placed — and the maximum reads 4 off the crest: midline 1 plus amplitude 3. Each dial moved one feature and left the others alone; that separation IS the anatomy of the sinusoid.
widget.lowFeedback: Keep adjusting — compare your wave against the dashed target one feature at a time.
widget.highFeedback: Keep adjusting — compare your wave against the dashed target one feature at a time.

explanationVariants: The wave swings 3 below the midline 1: down to −2.

widget.prompt: Same function. What is the MINIMUM value?

commonErrors.feedback: Subtract the amplitude FROM the midline: 1 − 3 = −2, not 3 − 1.
−3 would be the min around midline 0. This wave rides midline 1: min −2.

explanationVariants: The sine shape starts (midline, rising) at x = C = π/4; it peaks a quarter-period later. Period = π, quarter = π/4: peak at π/4 + π/4 = π/2.
Peak where 2(x − π/4) = π/2: x − π/4 = π/4, x = π/2.

widget.prompt: Same function: y = 3 sin(2(x − π/4)) + 1. Where is its first peak for x ≥ 0?

options.label: x = π/2
options.feedback: Right — start at the shift π/4, climb a quarter-period (π/4) to the crest.

options.label: x = π/4
options.feedback: π/4 is where the wave CROSSES the midline going up (the sine start). The peak comes a quarter-period later: π/2.

options.label: x = π
options.feedback: π is a half-period past the start — the wave is back at the midline heading DOWN. The peak is at π/2.

steps.body: Going the other way — **reading a graph** — use the landmarks in this order: midline D = (max + min)/2; amplitude A = (max − min)/2; period from repeat-distance, then B = 2π/period; finally C = where a rising midline-crossing sits.

explanationVariants: Midline halfway between the extremes: 4; swing: 3.

widget.prompt: A sinusoid oscillates between a max of 7 and a min of 1. What is its midline D?

commonErrors.feedback: 3 is the AMPLITUDE (7 − 1)/2. The midline AVERAGES the extremes: (7 + 1)/2 = 4.

explanationVariants: A = (9 − 1)/2 = 4, D = 5, period 6π → B = 2π/(6π) = 1/3, rising midline-crossing at x = π → C = π. Rule: 4 sin((1/3)(x − π)) + 5; B as a decimal ≈ 0.33.
hints: B comes only from the period: B = 2π/period.

widget.prompt: A wave has max 9, min 1, period 6π, and a rising midline-crossing at x = π. In y = A sin(B(x − C)) + D, what is B? (Round to hundredths.)

commonErrors.feedback: 3 would give period 2π/3. Period 6π needs B = 2π/(6π) = 1/3 ≈ 0.33.
6 is the period's coefficient of π, not B. B = 2π ÷ 6π = 1/3.
4 is the AMPLITUDE. B is the period dial: 1/3 ≈ 0.33.

takeaways: Max/min = D ± A; period = 2π/B; start the shape at x = C.
Reading a graph: D and A from extremes, B from the period, C from a rising crossing.
Peaks sit a quarter-period after each rising midline-crossing.
steps.teaser: Next: cosine joins in — and turns out to be a shifted sine.

concept.body: Landmark order for reading: D = (max+min)/2 → A = (max−min)/2 → B = 2π/period → C from a rising midline-crossing.

widget.prompt: A sinusoid runs between 10 and 2. What is its amplitude A?

commonErrors.feedback: 6 is the MIDLINE (10 + 2)/2. Amplitude halves the DIFFERENCE: (10 − 2)/2 = 4.
8 is the full swing; amplitude is half of it: 4.
